cases.scenario: Producer provenance quantity, household received quantity, accepted quantity and rejected quantity share mass dimension; accepted plus rejected equals received; ordered event chain accounts for consumption; remainder covers recipe requirement.
Received quantity is split into accepted and rejected quantities with exact same-dimension arithmetic; only accepted amount is available to recipe planning.
Producer lot and listing exist but no local receipt record is supplied; supplier availability is not household stock.
Receipt quantity arithmetic does not balance after exact same-dimension conversion; no quantity is allocated.
Accepted quantity is mass while rejected quantity is volume; no cross-dimension sum is inferred.
Recipe requires mass but received lot declares volume and no independently sourced exact conversion exists.
Append-only consumed events exceed accepted quantity; later allocation is blocked pending reconciliation.
Split event child receipt quantities plus parent remainder do not reconcile to the pre-split quantity.
An event sequence skips, duplicates a sequence, or references the wrong parent event; the chain cannot be treated as complete.
A child event timestamp precedes its parent beyond the declared clock policy; retain the conflict rather than silently sorting by time.
A recall notice event exists; mark the receipt unavailable pending authoritative disposition without asserting the food is unsafe.
The declared use-by timestamp has elapsed at the explicit reconciliation as_of time; do not represent lot as available for recipe planning.
Expiry-sensitive reconciliation is requested but no trustworthy as_of time is available.
Receipt or packaging reference points to an older lot revision while a newer exact revision is required by the selected workflow.
The same event reference or event identifier appears more than once in the local chain.
Listing/order references are present but no local physical receipt observation exists.
